t: A Bamana kingdom on the middle Niger, founded around 1712 by Biton Kulibali, who turned a young men’s association into an army.
Its power rested on the tonjon, soldiers of captive origin, and on the trade of Muslim Maraka towns such as Sinsani.
It resisted the Fulbe jihads until Umar Tall took Ségou in 1861; its kings live on in the griots’ epics.
dyk: When Mungo Park reached Ségou in 1796, King Monzon (Mansong) would not receive him but sent him 5,000 cowries to buy food for his journey.
ev: Biton Kulibali turns the ton of Ségou into an army and makes himself king
Biton defeats Kaarta’s Massassi rulers and captures their king, Foulakoro
Ngolo Diarra, a former tonjon, seizes power and founds the Diarra dynasty
Mungo Park reaches the Niger at Ségou during the reign of Monzon Diarra
Seku Amadu’s victory at Noukouma begins the Massina jihad that takes Djenné
Umar Tall’s army defeats the Bamana at Woïtala
Umar Tall takes Ségou and makes it the capital of the Toucouleur Empire

f.capital: Ségou (Ségou-Koro under Biton; Ségou-Sikoro under the Diarra kings)
f.predecessor: Bamana chiefdoms of the Ségou region
